pois.name: Edinburgh Waverley
pois.blurb: Edinburgh Waverley railway station opened in 1866 and remains the principal railway station serving scheduled passenger trains in Edinburgh.

themeConnection.text: The station site entered passenger railway use in 1866 and remains an active central-city station.

pois.name: St Pancras International
pois.blurb: St Pancras International () is a major central London railway terminus on Euston Road in the London Borough of Camden. It is the terminus for Eurostar services from Belgium, France and the Netherlands to the UK.

themeConnection.text: Passenger railway service began at the site in 1868, and the station remains an active heavy-rail terminal.

pois.name: Praha hlavní nádraží
pois.blurb: Praha hlavní nádraží opened in 1871 and continues to serve scheduled domestic and international passenger railway services.

themeConnection.text: The station site began passenger railway service in 1871 and remains Prague's principal active rail station.

pois.name: Brighton railway station
pois.blurb: Brighton railway station opened in 1840 and continues to provide regular scheduled passenger services in the city.

themeConnection.text: Brighton station opened in 1840 and remains an active public passenger railway station.

pois.name: Amsterdam Centraal
pois.blurb: Amsterdam Centraal railway station opened in 1889 and continues to handle regular domestic and international passenger trains.

themeConnection.text: Amsterdam Centraal opened in 1889 and remains the city's principal operating passenger railway station.

pois.name: Glasgow Central
pois.blurb: Glasgow Central station opened in 1879 and continues to operate as one of Scotland's busiest scheduled passenger railway stations.

themeConnection.text: The present station opened in 1879 and remains a major active passenger railway terminus.

pois.name: Gare du Nord
pois.blurb: The Gare du Nord (pronounced [ɡaʁ dy nɔːʁ]; English: North Station), officially Paris-Nord, is one of the seven large mainline railway station termini in Paris, France, and Europe's busiest railway station.

themeConnection.text: The first Gare du Nord opened in 1846; the present station site remains an active heavy-rail terminal.

pois.name: Bern railway station
pois.blurb: Bern railway station opened in 1858 and remains an active central Swiss station serving regular national and international passengers.

themeConnection.text: Bern's railway station opened in 1858 and continues to serve scheduled passenger trains.

pois.name: Kraków Główny
pois.blurb: Kraków Główny railway station opened in 1847 and continues to serve regular scheduled passenger trains in central Kraków.

themeConnection.text: The station opened in 1847 and remains an operating heavy-rail passenger station.

pois.name: Liverpool Lime Street
pois.blurb: Liverpool Lime Street station opened in 1836 and is the city's main railway terminus, with continuing scheduled passenger services.

themeConnection.text: The station opened in 1836 and continues to handle scheduled intercity and regional passenger trains.

pois.name: Sofia Central Station
pois.blurb: The Sofia Central Railway Station (Bulgarian: Централна железопътна гара София, romanized: Tsentralna zhelezopatna gara Sofiya) is the main passenger railway station of Sofia, the capital of Bulgaria, as well as the largest railway station in the country.

themeConnection.text: The station opened in 1888 and remains the principal operating heavy-rail passenger terminal in Sofia.

pois.name: Ljubljana railway station
pois.blurb: Ljubljana railway station opened in 1849 and continues to serve regularly scheduled domestic and international passenger trains.

themeConnection.text: The station opened in 1849 and remains the operating principal passenger railway station of Ljubljana.

pois.name: Wrocław Główny
pois.blurb: Wrocław Główny railway station opened in 1842 and remains a busy operating station for scheduled regional and long-distance trains.

themeConnection.text: Passenger railway service began in 1842, and the station remains an active city terminal.

pois.name: Stockholm Central Station
pois.blurb: Stockholm Central Station (Swedish: Stockholms centralstation), is the main railway station in Stockholm, and largest railway station in Sweden in terms of passenger numbers and train traffic.

themeConnection.text: Stockholm Central opened in 1871 and remains the city's active main-line passenger station.

themeConnection.text: Keleti station opened in 1884 and remains an active Budapest passenger terminal.

pois.name: Zürich Hauptbahnhof
pois.blurb: Zürich Hauptbahnhof, often shortened to Zürich HB or just HB, and known in English as Zurich Main Station, is the largest railway station in Switzerland and one of the busiest in Europe.

themeConnection.text: The first station opened in 1847, and the present site remains Switzerland's principal active passenger terminal.

themeConnection.text: Bucharest North opened in 1872 and remains the city's active main passenger railway terminal.

theme.title: Operating Pre-1900 Railway Stations in Cities
theme.introduction: Steel, glass, and old platforms gather the world’s city stories. Find stations where yesterday’s railways still welcome today’s travelers.
theme.inclusionCriteria: Include a location only when every condition is met: (1) it is an individually named heavy-rail passenger station or terminal; (2) the station or its immediately identifiable predecessor began railway passenger service at the same site on or before 31 December 1899; (3) regularly scheduled public passenger trains currently serve that station on the date of play; (4) the station occupies a fixed, mappable site with a recognizable public entrance or concourse; (5) it lies within the current administrative boundary of a present-day city or incorporated urban municipality; and (6) the exact station, rather than an entire rail district or line, can be used as the game location. Plausible locations include St Pancras International, King’s Cross, London Paddington, London Waterloo, Liverpool Lime Street, Manchester Victoria, Glasgow Central, Edinburgh Waverley, York railway station, Bristol Temple Meads, Brighton railway station, Gare du Nord, Gare de l’Est, Gare Saint-Lazare, Gare d’Austerlitz, Amsterdam Centraal, Zürich Hauptbahnhof, Bern railway station, Stockholm Central Station, Kraków Główny, Wrocław Główny, Prague Main Railway Station, Budapest Keleti, Budapest Nyugati, Ljubljana railway station, Bratislava hlavná stanica, București Nord, Sofia Central Station, Roma Termini, Wien Praterstern, Trieste Centrale, Leningradsky railway station, Sirkeci railway station, Ramses Station, Alexandria Misr railway station, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Sealdah railway station, Chennai Central, Rio de Janeiro Central do Brasil, Buenos Aires Constitución, and Buenos Aires Once.
